solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Jumper Mark has got hold of without assistance?

indicators.note: one word gripping another, so the mark's letters wrap round the second piece

parts.note: a pock is a pit or scar mark on the skin, as in pockmark
doing something alone is doing it unaided

explanation.surface: A question about a man named Mark managing to grab something all by himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name but is a skin blemish. A polo neck is a British name for a jumper with a high rolled collar (a turtleneck).
explanation.definitionFit: Jumper is British for sweater, and this is a sweater style with a tall folded collar.

clue.text: Operated by pressure, plug still not coming up

parts.note: to plug a product is to push or promote it
still and but both mean nevertheless

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the word not taken as written, then turned

explanation.surface: Pressing something, yet a plug still refuses to rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A device of this kind is worked by pressing it, so it is pressure-activated.

clue.text: Light was at the front

definitions.meaning: a light-emitting diode is a small electronic lamp
past tense of being ahead, as a race leader

explanation.definitionFit: A diode lamp is called by its initials, and the past tense of lead means was ahead.

clue.text: Long time taken up securing pit candidate

indicators.note: holding firmly, so the reversed long time goes round the pit
in a down entry, raised up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: an eon is an immensely long period
a mine is a pit dug for coal

explanation.surface: A long stretch spent securing a coal pit for a candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns EON into NOE, which holds MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone put forward for office or an award is a proposed candidate.

clue.text: Distributed vast incomes to defend right political ideology

indicators.note: defending is guarding round something, so the jumble surrounds the letter for right
spread around, so the letters of the two words are shared out in a new order

explanation.surface: Sharing out great wealth to protect right-wing thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distributed' scrambles VAST INCOMES; 'to defend' puts it round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A belief in tradition and limited change is the doctrine of the political right.

clue.text: Wielding this could make you chesty

definitions.text: Wielding this could make you chesty

indicators.note: wielding means handling or working over, so the letters of chesty are worked into a new order; read in reverse, working the blade's letters makes chesty

explanation.surface: A warning that using some tool might leave you with a cough.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: 'Wielding' the letters of 'this' (the answer) makes CHESTY, so the letters of 'chesty' rearranged give the tool. Swinging one would broaden your chest too.
explanation.definitionFit: A long curved blade on a pole, swung by hand to cut grass or corn, is the tool meant.

clue.text: Court official, firm one belted by bishop?

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: with a belt round it, so the bishop's letters encircle one

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A firm figure of the court who is struck by a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belted by' looks like hit but means wrapped round. In Britain this official holds inquests into unexplained deaths.
explanation.definitionFit: This official presides over a court of inquest, so is a legal officer.

clue.text: A couple of Poles taken in by purchase deal

indicators.note: being taken in is being put inside, so the purchase surrounds the other letters

parts.note: purchase is grip or traction
North and South, N and S, are the two poles

explanation.surface: Two Polish people deceived by a business purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' are not people but the Earth's poles; 'purchase' is grip, not buying.
explanation.definitionFit: A business deal or exchange is a commercial operation of that kind.

clue.text: Waste carrier avoids small vessel

indicators.note: keeping away from, so the letter for small is dropped

parts.note: a sewer carries waste water

explanation.surface: A drain that steers clear of a little boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' looks like a ship but is a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large water jug, so a container, a vessel for liquid.

clue.text: Staff in courses on reflection settled matter

indicators.note: one piece placed within another, so the staff go inside the courses
reflected as in a mirror, so the word for courses is read backwards

parts.note: tides are the courses or flows of the sea
staff are the workers, the men

explanation.surface: Workers on training courses thinking back over things that were decided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns TIDES into SEDIT, and MEN goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is solid material that has sunk and settled at the bottom of a liquid.

clue.text: Make box for holding tablet

indicators.note: the box contains the tablet, so its letters go round the other piece

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box for goods
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: Instructions to build a box to keep a pill or a stone slab in.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something is to bring it into being, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Wow! Is sauce included in awful local dish?

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: being put inside, so the awful word surrounds the next pieces

parts.note: nasty means awful
HP is a British brand of brown sauce

explanation.surface: Surprise that sauce is part of a horrible regional dish.
explanation.walkthrough: HP is a famous British bottled brown sauce. The answer is a pastry turnover of meat and vegetables from Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the traditional pie of one English county, so a regional dish.

clue.text: Cake aims to get awards

parts.note: a brownie is a small rich chocolate cake
to point something is to aim it

explanation.surface: A cake hoping to win prizes, as at a baking contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit earned for good deeds, notional marks of favour, is an idiom for small rewards.

clue.text: About ten monkeys playing with gas — from these?

definitions.text: About ten monkeys playing with gas — from these?

indicators.note: around, so the jumbled letters go round the ten
playing with means fooling around, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A troop of monkeys messing about with gas, which these would protect against.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a hint: the gas the wearer breathes comes from these.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing apparatus supplies the gas to the wearer, so the gas comes from these.

clue.text: Stubborn little chap drank bottles

indicators.note: to bottle is to enclose, so the word for drank holds the little chap

parts.note: swilled means drank greedily
an elf is a small fairy fellow

explanation.surface: An obstinate small man knocked back the bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' looks like the drinks but is a verb meaning contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Insisting on one's own way regardless is headstrong, which is obstinate.

clue.text: Ingredient of healthy meals?

indicators.note: an ingredient is a part of a mixture, so the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Asking what goes into nutritious cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: The herb is buried across 'healthy meals', and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The herb is a common cooking ingredient, so it is literally part of many meals.

clue.text: Express anger about constant cavity

parts.note: to vent a feeling is to express it

indicators.note: one word surrounding another, so the anger goes round the constant

parts.note: to rile is to anger
c is the usual symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: Letting off steam about something that never changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express anger' looks like one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a hollow chamber of the heart or brain, so a cavity in anatomy.

clue.text: Works of obscure poetaster

indicators.note: to obscure is to confuse or blur, so these letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: The writings of a little-known bad poet.
explanation.walkthrough: A poetaster is a writer of feeble verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Light operas are musical stage works, so the definition is one example of a kind of creative output.

clue.text: Foreign articles extremely likely to be getting on

parts.note: el is the Spanish and der the German for the, two articles side by side

indicators.note: only the outer letters, the extremes, are taken

explanation.surface: Imported goods are very likely to be making progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on is an idiom for growing old, so it is a fair stand-in for aged.

clue.text: Cheese fondue's first for barman?

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: only the opening letter of fondue is taken

explanation.surface: A cheese fondue, starting point for someone serving behind a pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barman' is not a bartender but a member of the Bar: in Britain a brief is slang for a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Barristers belong to the Bar, so a barman here is a lawyer, colloquially called a brief.

clue.text: Citizen's food sent up with woman's

definitions.note: read as citizen is, the apostrophe-s being a link

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending something up reverses the word

parts.note: grub is slang for food
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A citizen's meal sent back with a lady's order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Citizen's' is read as 'citizen is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A burgher is a town dweller with civic rights, an old word for a citizen.

clue.text: This method briefly doing for a medic?

definitions.text: This method briefly doing for a medic?

parts.words: This method briefly doing for a medic?
parts.note: the short form MO stands both for this Latin phrase for a way of working and for a medical officer

explanation.surface: A question about a shortened procedure standing in for a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: MO abbreviates both the Latin working method and Medical Officer, so the method's abbreviation 'does for' (substitutes for) a medic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means a characteristic way of operating, so a method.

clue.text: Wood popular in gym

indicators.note: placed within, so the word for popular goes inside the gym

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A favourite timber used in the gymnasium.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the soft timber of a conifer tree, so a type of wood.

clue.text: Cover one name of course

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
of course and sure both mean certainly

explanation.surface: Covering a single name on a golf course or race course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like a place but is an interjection meaning certainly.
explanation.definitionFit: To insure property is to take out a policy that covers it against loss.

clue.text: Plant takes a short while to camouflage brick container

indicators.note: hiding something by covering it, so the first letters wrap round the container
cut short, the last letter is dropped from the word for a while

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
a hod is the trough a builder carries bricks in

explanation.surface: A plant soon hides a builder's brick holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the last letter, leaving SPEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily-family flower, in myth the flower of the Elysian fields.

clue.text: Spot one of three in Fiji

definitions.meaning: the word Fiji, written in lower case, has three small marks above its letters i, j and i

explanation.definitionFit: A tiny round mark is a spot, and the letters i and j each carry one.

clue.text: Studies state on board English ship

indicators.note: being aboard a vessel, so the word for state goes inside the ship

parts.note: SS is steamship
to state is to say

explanation.surface: Studies a nation's place on an English ship's board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a noun (a country) but is the verb SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A study can be a short piece of written analysis on a topic, which is a composition of that kind.

clue.text: Part-time doctor and daughter keeping swine supplied with water

indicators.note: holding something within, so the first pieces surround the swine

parts.note: Mr Hyde is the other self of Dr Jekyll, so the man is only a doctor part of the time
a rat is a contemptible person, as is a swine

explanation.surface: A locum and his daughter keeping pigs and giving them water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swine' is not a pig but a rotter; Mr Hyde is Dr Jekyll's other self, hence a part-time doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hydrated is to have had enough water taken in, a direct synonym.
